name: Vermouth
description: Wine that has been fortified and flavoured with wormwood and other botanicals. Styles run from dry and pale to sweet and red, and it is a core modifier in stirred drinks.

name: Sweet Vermouth
description: Red, sweetened vermouth in the Italian style, coloured with caramel and spiced with wormwood, citrus peel and vanilla. The vermouth of the Manhattan and the Negroni.

name: Dry Vermouth
description: Pale vermouth with little sugar and a herbal, lightly bitter profile, in the French style. The vermouth of the Martini, and also used for cooking.

name: Bianco Vermouth
description: Clear, sweet white vermouth, called bianco in Italy and blanc in France. Softer and more floral than dry vermouth, often with vanilla and citrus notes.

name: Rosé Vermouth
description: Pink vermouth made on rosé wine or a blend of white and red wines. Usually semi-sweet, with red fruit, citrus and spice, and often served in a spritz.

name: Ambrato Vermouth
description: Amber vermouth that sits between bianco and rosso in colour and sweetness. It tends to taste of honey, chamomile and dried citrus with a gentle bitterness.

name: Vermouth di Torino
description: Vermouth made in Piedmont under a protected geographical indication, using Italian wine and Piedmontese wormwood. It covers dry, bianco and rosso styles.

name: Quinquina
description: Aromatised wine bittered with cinchona bark, the source of quinine. A French aperitif style that includes Lillet, Byrrh and Dubonnet, used like a light vermouth.

name: Americano
description: Italian aromatised wine bittered with gentian as well as wormwood and citrus. More bitter than vermouth, it is served over ice with soda or used in place of a quinquina.

name: Aperitif Wine
description: A broad family of wines that are flavoured or fortified and served before a meal. It covers vermouth, quinquina, americano and fruit or mistelle styles.

name: Pineau des Charentes
description: A mistelle from the Cognac region made by adding young cognac to unfermented grape juice, then ageing it in oak. Sweet, with flavours of honey, stone fruit and nuts.

name: Macvin du Jura
description: A mistelle from the Jura in eastern France, made from grape must fortified with local marc brandy and aged in oak. Sweet, with raisin, quince and walnut notes.

name: Sherry
description: Fortified wine from the Jerez region of southern Spain, aged in a solera system. Styles range from pale, bone dry fino to dark, sweet Pedro Ximénez.

name: Fino Sherry
description: The palest and driest sherry, aged under a layer of flor yeast that keeps it fresh. It tastes of almond, bread dough and green apple with a saline edge.

name: Manzanilla Sherry
description: A fino style sherry aged only in the coastal town of Sanlúcar de Barrameda. Very dry and light, with chamomile, green olive and a salty finish.

name: Amontillado Sherry
description: Sherry that starts life under flor like a fino and then ages with oxygen. Dry and amber coloured, with hazelnut, caramel and dried herb flavours.

name: Oloroso Sherry
description: Sherry aged entirely with oxygen and no flor, which makes it dark, full bodied and dry. It tastes of walnut, dried fruit, leather and toffee.

name: Palo Cortado Sherry
description: A rare dry sherry that loses its flor early and then ages with oxygen. It combines the aroma of an amontillado with the weight of an oloroso.

name: Pedro Ximénez Sherry
description: Very sweet, almost black sherry made from sun dried Pedro Ximénez grapes. Thick and syrupy, with raisin, fig, molasses and coffee flavours.

name: Cream Sherry
description: Sweet blended sherry, usually oloroso sweetened with Pedro Ximénez or grape must. Smooth and rich, with dried fruit, caramel and nut flavours.

name: Moscatel Sherry
description: Sweet sherry made from Moscatel grapes, often from vineyards near Chipiona. Floral and honeyed, with orange blossom, raisin and citrus peel flavours.

name: Port
description: Sweet fortified wine from the Douro Valley in northern Portugal. Grape spirit is added during fermentation, which keeps natural sugar and raises the strength.

name: Ruby Port
description: Young red port aged a few years in large vats so it keeps its deep colour and fresh fruit. Sweet, with blackberry, cherry and plum flavours.

name: Tawny Port
description: Port aged in small oak casks, where it fades to amber brown and takes on nutty flavours. Sweet, with caramel, dried fig, walnut and orange peel.

name: White Port
description: Port made from white grapes, in styles from dry to sweet. It is golden, with citrus, almond and honey notes, and is often mixed with tonic water.

name: Late Bottled Vintage Port
description: Red port from a single year that is aged four to six years in wood before bottling. Fuller and more structured than ruby, with dark fruit and spice.

name: Madeira
description: Fortified wine from the Portuguese island of Madeira that is deliberately heated and oxidised as it ages. High in acid, with caramel, nut and citrus peel flavours.

name: Rainwater Madeira
description: A lighter, medium dry style of Madeira, usually made from Tinta Negra grapes. Pale amber and gently nutty, it is the style most often called for in old punch recipes.

name: Marsala
description: Fortified wine from the west of Sicily, made dry, semi-dry or sweet and in gold, amber or ruby colours. It tastes of dried apricot, vanilla and brown sugar.

name: Amaro
description: Italian bittersweet herbal liqueur, traditionally served after a meal. Each one steeps its own mix of roots, barks, herbs and citrus peel in spirit or wine and adds sugar.

name: Bitter Aperitivo
description: Bright red or orange bittersweet liqueur in the Italian aperitivo style, flavoured with bitter orange, rhubarb and gentian. The base of the Negroni and the spritz.

name: Bitter Bianco
description: A clear version of the Italian red bitter, made without colouring. Citrus led and firmly bitter, it is used for white Negroni style drinks.

name: Fernet
description: A dry, intensely bitter style of amaro with very little sugar. Typical flavours are menthol, saffron, myrrh, aloe and gentian. Drunk as a shot or in small measures.

name: Carciofo
description: Amaro flavoured with artichoke leaves along with other herbs and roots. Dark and vegetal with a bittersweet, slightly earthy taste. Cynar is the best known example.

name: Rabarbaro
description: Amaro based on Chinese rhubarb root, which is dried and gives a smoky, earthy bitterness. Dark in colour and usually lower in strength than other amari.

name: Gentian Aperitif
description: French liqueur flavoured mainly with the root of yellow gentian from the Massif Central. Pale yellow, earthy and sharply bitter, with a floral, citrus edge.

name: Bitter Liqueur
description: Herbal bitter liqueurs from outside the Italian amaro tradition, such as the digestif bitters of Central and Northern Europe. Usually dark, strong and lightly sweetened.

name: Carpano Antica Formula
description: Rich Italian sweet vermouth based on a Carpano recipe dated 1786. Marked vanilla, with cocoa, dried fruit and bitter orange. A bartender standard for Manhattans.

name: Punt e Mes
description: Dark Italian vermouth from Carpano with an extra dose of bitter quina. Sweet at first, then firmly bitter, with orange peel and cocoa notes.

name: Carpano Classico Rosso Vermouth
description: The everyday red vermouth from Carpano. Medium sweet, with orange peel, clove and caramel, and lighter on vanilla than Antica Formula.

name: Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino
description: Sweet vermouth from Asti made on Moscato wine to Giulio Cocchi's 1891 recipe. Cocoa, rhubarb and bitter orange with a balanced, lightly bitter finish.
image_query: Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino bottle

name: Cocchi Americano

name: Cocchi Americano Rosa

name: Dubonnet

name: Bonal Gentiane-Quina

description: Sweet white port from Graham's made from traditional Douro white grapes. Golden, with almond, citrus and honey flavours. Served chilled or with tonic.

name: Taylor's Late Bottled Vintage Port
description: Red port from a single year, aged four to six years in wood. Taylor's created the modern style and it is the largest selling example. Blackcurrant, cherry and spice.
image_query: Taylor's Late Bottled Vintage Port bottle

name: Taylor's 10 Year Old Tawny Port
description: Tawny port from Taylor's with an average age of ten years in oak. Amber brown, with dried fig, walnut, butterscotch and a smooth, mellow finish.
image_query: Taylor's 10 Year Old Tawny Port bottle

name: Taylor's Chip Dry White Port
description: Dry white port introduced by Taylor's in 1934, made mostly from Malvasia Fina grapes. Crisp and nutty. The classic choice for a port and tonic.
image_query: Taylor's Chip Dry White Port bottle

name: Fonseca Bin 27 Port
description: Reserve ruby port from Fonseca, aged about four years in large wooden vats. Deep ruby, with blackberry, cassis, cherry and plum and a velvety texture.

name: Sandeman Fine Ruby Port
description: Entry level ruby port from Sandeman, a house founded in 1790. Bright red and sweet, with fresh plum and red berry fruit. A common pouring port.

name: Sandeman Fine Tawny Port
description: Entry level tawny port from Sandeman, lighter in colour and body than the ruby. Sweet, with vanilla, dried fruit and a gentle nutty note.

name: Cockburn's Special Reserve Port
description: Reserve ruby port launched in 1969, aged longer in oak than a standard ruby. Sweet and smooth, with red cherry, plum and a drier finish. A leading seller in the UK.

name: Cockburn's Fine Ruby Port
description: Young ruby port from Cockburn's, aged up to three years in oak vats. Bright and fruity, with red berries and cherry. Suited to mixing and cooking.

name: Dow's Fine Ruby Port
description: Young ruby port from Dow's, a house known for a slightly drier style. Fresh and full, with blackberry and cherry fruit and a peppery finish.

name: Warre's Warrior Reserve Port
description: Reserve ruby port from Warre's, shipped under the Warrior name since the 1750s. Full bodied and sweet, with ripe plum, black cherry and firm tannin.

name: Warre's Otima 10 Year Old Tawny Port
description: Ten year old tawny port from Warre's, sold in a clear 50 cl bottle. Lighter and fresher than most tawnies, with dried fruit, hazelnut and orange peel.
image_query: Warre's Otima 10 Year Old Tawny Port bottle

name: Quinta do Noval Black Port
description: Reserve ruby port from Quinta do Noval, made in a fresher style for drinking chilled and for cocktails. Dark fruit, black cherry and dark chocolate.
image_query: Quinta do Noval Black Port bottle

name: Churchill's Dry White Port
description: White port from Churchill's, aged around ten years in oak, which is unusually long for the style. Golden, dry and nutty, with dried apricot and citrus peel.

name: Penfolds Club Tawny
description: Australian fortified tawny from Penfolds, blended from Shiraz, Mataro and Grenache and aged in old oak. Sweet, with raisin, toffee and nut flavours.

name: Blandy's Duke of Clarence Rich Madeira
description: Sweet, full bodied Madeira from Blandy's made from Tinta Negra grapes and aged three years in oak. Flavours of raisin, toffee and dried fig with balancing acidity.
image_query: Blandy's Duke of Clarence Rich Madeira bottle

name: Blandy's 5 Year Old Malmsey Madeira
description: Sweet Madeira made from Malvasia grapes and aged five years in American oak in the canteiro method. Rich, with honey, raisin, toffee and bright acidity.
image_query: Blandy's 5 Year Old Malmsey Madeira bottle

name: Blandy's Rainwater Madeira
description: Medium dry rainwater Madeira from Blandy's, made from Tinta Negra and aged three years. Pale gold and light, with dried fruit, nut and a fresh, tangy finish.

name: Henriques & Henriques Rainwater Madeira
description: Medium dry rainwater Madeira aged three years, from a house founded in 1850. Light amber, with orange peel, almond and caramel and a crisp, dry finish.

name: Henriques & Henriques 10 Year Old Sercial Madeira
description: Dry Madeira made from Sercial grapes and aged ten years in oak. High in acidity, with citrus peel, toasted almond and a long, sharp finish.
image_query: Henriques & Henriques 10 Year Old Sercial Madeira bottle

name: Florio Vecchioflorio Marsala Superiore Secco
description: Dry Marsala Superiore from Cantine Florio, founded in Marsala in 1833. Made from Grillo grapes and aged in oak. Amber, with dried apricot, vanilla and almond.
image_query: Florio Vecchioflorio Marsala Superiore Secco bottle

name: Pellegrino Marsala Superiore Garibaldi Dolce
description: Sweet Marsala Superiore from Cantine Pellegrino, aged at least two years in oak. Amber, with raisin, dried fig and caramel. Used for zabaglione, cooking and mixing.
image_query: Pellegrino Marsala Superiore Garibaldi Dolce bottle

name: Campari
description: The benchmark Italian red bitter, created by Gaspare Campari in 1860. Strongly bitter and sweet, with bitter orange, rhubarb and herbs. Essential in the Negroni and Americano.

name: Aperol
description: Bright orange Italian aperitivo created in Padua in 1919. Low in alcohol and mildly bitter, with sweet orange, rhubarb and gentian. The base of the Aperol Spritz.

name: Select Aperitivo
description: Red bitter aperitivo created in Venice in 1920 and the traditional choice for a Venetian spritz. Medium bitter, with rhubarb root, juniper and citrus.

name: Cappelletti Aperitivo
description: Wine based red bitter from Trentino, often called Specialino. Softer and less sweet than Campari, with bitter orange and herbs. Coloured with natural carmine.

name: Luxardo Bitter Rosso
description: Red bitter from Luxardo made by infusing bitter orange, rhubarb, mint, marjoram and thyme. Bittersweet and used like Campari in Negronis and spritzes.

name: Luxardo Bitter Bianco
description: Clear bitter from Luxardo made from the same botanicals as its red bitter, distilled and finished with wormwood. Citrus led and bitter, for white Negronis.

name: Luxardo Aperitivo
description: Light orange aperitivo from Luxardo, close to Aperol in style and strength. Sweet orange, rhubarb and mild bitter herbs. Made for the spritz.

name: Martini Riserva Speciale Bitter
description: Red bitter from Martini based on an 1872 recipe and rested in Tino casks. Flavoured with saffron, angostura bark and calumba. Rich, with a lasting bitterness.

name: Contratto Bitter
description: Red bitter from Contratto in Piedmont, based on a 1933 recipe and coloured with beetroot and carrot extracts. Bittersweet, with orange peel, clove and gentian.

name: Contratto Aperitif
description: Orange aperitivo from Contratto, based on a 1935 recipe and naturally coloured. Light and bittersweet, with orange, mandarin and rhubarb. An alternative to Aperol.

name: Gran Classico Bitter
description: Amber bitter from Tempus Fugit based on an 1860s Turin recipe and made without added colour. Bitter orange, gentian, rhubarb and wormwood with a rich, sweet body.
image_query: Gran Classico Bitter Tempus Fugit bottle

name: St. George Bruto Americano
description: Californian red bitter from St. George Spirits, flavoured with Seville orange, gentian and California buckthorn bark. Woody and bitter, coloured with cochineal.

name: Meletti 1870 Bitter
description: Red bitter from the Meletti family in Le Marche, made from sweet and bitter orange with gentian, coriander, cinnamon and clove. Bittersweet, for Negronis and spritzes.

name: Økar Island Bitter
description: Australian red bitter from Applewood Distillery in the Adelaide Hills, made with native riberry, Davidson plum and strawberry gum. Bittersweet and used like Campari.
image_query: Okar Island Bitter Applewood Distillery bottle

name: Poor Toms Imbroglio Amaro
description: Red bitter from Poor Toms distillery in Sydney, labelled Amaro Australiano. Flavoured with strawberry gum, bitter orange and gentian, and mixed like Campari.

name: Adelaide Hills Distillery Bitter Orange
description: Australian orange aperitif, also known as The Italian, made with local oranges and native botanicals including riberries. Bittersweet, for spritzes and Negronis.
image_query: Adelaide Hills Distillery The Italian Bitter Orange bottle

name: Amaro Montenegro
description: Light, approachable amaro made in Bologna since 1885 from 40 botanicals. Sweet orange peel, rose water, vanilla and coriander with only a gentle bitterness.

name: Averna
description: Sicilian amaro made in Caltanissetta since 1868. Dark, sweet and full bodied, with cola, liquorice, orange peel and a mild bitterness. Used in the Black Manhattan.

name: Amaro Nonino Quintessentia
description: Amaro from the Nonino family in Friuli, built on aged grape distillate. Lighter and drier than most, with orange, caramel and alpine herbs. Used in the Paper Plane.

name: Ramazzotti
description: Amaro first made in Milan in 1815 from 33 herbs and roots. Medium sweet, with cola, orange peel, star anise and cardamom and a moderate bitterness.

name: Amaro Lucano
description: Amaro from Pisticci in Basilicata, made since 1894 from more than 30 herbs. Balanced between sweet and bitter, with caramel, citrus peel, wormwood and gentian.

name: Meletti Amaro
description: Amaro from Ascoli Piceno in Le Marche. Sweet and gently bitter, with saffron, anise, violet, clove and caramel. A common mixing amaro in American bars.

name: Amaro CioCiaro
description: Amaro from the Paolucci family in Lazio, made since 1873. Dark and bittersweet, with burnt orange and cola notes. Often used as a stand in for Amer Picon.

name: Braulio
description: Alpine amaro made in Bormio in the Valtellina since 1875 and aged in Slavonian oak. Piney and mentholated, with juniper, gentian, wormwood and yarrow.

name: Vecchio Amaro del Capo
description: Calabrian amaro from Distilleria Caffo, made from 29 local herbs, flowers and fruits. Sweet, with orange, liquorice and mint. Traditionally served ice cold from the freezer.

name: Cappelletti Sfumato Rabarbaro
description: Rabarbaro amaro from Cappelletti in Trentino, made with Chinese rhubarb root and alpine herbs. Smoky, earthy and bittersweet. Often paired with whisky or mezcal.

name: Zucca Rabarbaro
description: Milanese rhubarb amaro created in 1845 and made with Chinese rhubarb root, cardamom and bitter orange. Dark, lightly smoky and bittersweet. Classic with soda.

name: Cardamaro
description: Wine based amaro from Bosca in Piedmont, flavoured with cardoon and blessed thistle and aged in oak. Soft and nutty, closer to a sweet vermouth or an oloroso sherry.

name: Cappelletti Pasubio Vino Amaro
description: Wine based alpine amaro from Trentino, flavoured with mountain blueberries, pine and herbs of the Dolomites. Fruity, resinous and gently bitter.

name: Amaro Sibilla
description: Amaro from Varnelli in Le Marche, made since 1868 by decocting gentian and cinchona over a wood fire and sweetening with mountain honey. Dry, earthy and very bitter.

name: Amaro dell'Erborista
description: Unfiltered amaro from Varnelli, sweetened only with honey from the Sibillini mountains. Cloudy and dry, with rhubarb, gentian, sandalwood and a strong bitterness.

name: Amaro Nardini
description: Amaro from the Nardini grappa distillery in Bassano del Grappa. Dark and medium sweet, with bitter orange, peppermint, gentian and a liquorice finish.

name: Amaro di Angostura
description: Amaro from the House of Angostura in Trinidad, built on the same botanicals as its aromatic bitters. Flavours of cinnamon, dark chocolate, liquorice and clove.

name: Amaro Santa Maria al Monte
description: Strong, dry amaro in a Ligurian monastic style, close to a fernet. Flavours of aloe, myrrh, rhubarb, gentian and ginseng with a long, bitter, minty finish.
image_query: Amaro Santa Maria al Monte bottle

name: Amaro dell'Etna
description: Sicilian amaro made to a 1901 recipe from more than 26 herbs grown around Mount Etna. Full and spicy, with bitter orange, liquorice, cinnamon and vanilla.

name: Amara Amaro d'Arancia Rossa
description: Sicilian amaro made from the peel of blood oranges grown on the slopes of Mount Etna, with local herbs. Bright orange flavour, medium sweet and lightly bitter.

name: Luxardo Amaro Abano
description: Amaro from Luxardo named after the spa town of Abano Terme near Padua. Medium bodied, with cardamom, cinnamon, bitter orange peel and a peppery finish.

name: Amaro Tosolini
description: Amaro from the Tosolini distillery in Friuli, made by steeping Mediterranean herbs in grape spirit and resting in ash casks. Bitter orange, rosemary and spice.

name: Bigallet China-China Amer
description: French bitter orange liqueur made since 1875 from sweet and bitter orange peels, gentian and cinchona. Dark and bittersweet. A full strength stand in for Amer Picon.

name: Amer Picon
description: French bitter orange liqueur created in 1837, flavoured with orange peel, gentian and cinchona. Now sold mainly as Picon Bière for adding to beer. Called for in the Brooklyn.

name: Cynar
description: Italian amaro launched in 1952, made from 13 herbs and plants led by artichoke leaf. Dark, bittersweet and vegetal. Served with soda or used in place of Campari.

name: Cynar 70
description: A stronger, 70 proof version of Cynar released in 2015. The same artichoke based recipe with more intensity and less apparent sweetness. Suited to stirred drinks.

name: Fernet-Branca
description: The defining fernet, made in Milan since 1845 from 27 herbs and spices and aged a year in oak. Intensely bitter and minty, with saffron, myrrh and chamomile.

name: Branca Menta
description: A sweeter, mint forward version of Fernet-Branca, launched in the 1960s with added Piedmontese peppermint oil. Served over ice or with cola.

name: Fernet Hunter
description: A lighter, less sweet fernet made in Austria by the Holzer family. Flavours of arnica, orris root, lavender and ginseng. Popular in bars across Asia and Australia.

name: Fernet-Vallet
description: Mexican fernet first made in the 1860s by French emigrant Henri Vallet. Dark and very bitter, with cardamom, clove, cinnamon, quassia and gentian.

name: Luxardo Fernet
description: Fernet from Luxardo, made to a recipe from 1889. Dry and strongly bitter, with liquorice, cardamom, cinnamon, saffron and gentian, and less menthol than Fernet-Branca.

name: Suze
description: French gentian aperitif created in 1889. Bright yellow and bittersweet, with earthy gentian root, citrus and floral notes. The bitter element of the White Negroni.

name: Salers Gentiane Aperitif
description: Gentian aperitif from the Massif Central, made since 1885 and the oldest of its kind. Pale straw in colour, drier and more earthy than Suze, with a vegetal bitterness.

name: Avèze
description: Gentian liqueur from the Auvergne, made since 1929 from fresh gentian roots gathered in the regional volcano park. Golden, softer and sweeter than Salers.

name: Lo-Fi Gentian Amaro
description: Californian wine based amaro flavoured with gentian root, cinchona bark, hibiscus, grapefruit and ginger. Pink, fruity and bittersweet. Made for spritzes.

name: Beechworth Bitters The Daisy Age Amaro
description: Floral Australian amaro from Beechworth in Victoria, made with 15 flowers including daisy, violet, jasmine and elderflower. Bittered with artichoke and dandelion.
image_query: Beechworth Bitters The Daisy Age amaro bottle

name: Beechworth Bitters In The Weeds
description: Strong Australian herbal liqueur inspired by European monastic styles. Made with nettle, dandelion, citrus leaves and gum leaves grown or foraged around Beechworth.
image_query: Beechworth Bitters In The Weeds bottle

name: Unicum
description: Hungarian herbal bitter made by the Zwack family since 1790 from more than 40 herbs and aged in oak. Dark, dry and very bitter. Usually taken as a chilled shot.

name: Becherovka
description: Czech herbal liqueur made in Karlovy Vary since 1807. Bittersweet, with cinnamon, clove, ginger and anise. Served cold as a shot or mixed with tonic as a Beton.

name: Underberg
description: German herbal bitter made in Rheinberg since 1846 and sold in single serve 20 ml bottles wrapped in paper. Very bitter, with clove, anise and gentian.

name: Riga Black Balsam
description: Latvian herbal bitter made since 1752 from 24 botanicals and sold in a ceramic bottle. Black, bittersweet and intense, with birch bud, ginger and burnt caramel.

name: Jeppson's Malört
description: Chicago wormwood liqueur in the Swedish bäsk style, made since the 1930s. Dry and sharply bitter, with a grapefruit pith finish. Taken as a shot.
